ATL.name: Jock Landale
ATL.note: Landale (hip) won't play Sunday against the Pistons.
ATL.long: This will be Landale's fourth consecutive game on the inactive list. His next chance to play will come Friday in Boston.

ATL.name: Asa Newell
ATL.note: Newell underwent surgery Tuesday for a plantar plate tear in his left great toe, and he will be re-evaluated in approximately four months, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
ATL.long: Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

ATL.name: CJ McCollum
ATL.note: McCollum (calf) will miss at least four weeks, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network.
ATL.long: The veteran combo guard has been diagnosed with a left calf strain, and he's in line to miss the next month or so. Once rookie first-rounder Kingston Flemings (back) is healthy, he'll have a long runway as Atlanta's top point guard. Aaron Wiggins remains worth holding in nearly all fantasy leagues as well.

ATL.name: Mouhamed Gueye
ATL.note: Gueye (foot) is ready to begin on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
ATL.long: The team stated in July that the big man would remain sidelined for the next 3-to-4 months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot, and he's continuing to make progress in his rehab. A timetable for Gueye's 2026-27 debut has yet to be established, thought a date could come into focus following his next evaluation in mid-December.

ATL.name: Henri Veesaar
ATL.note: Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.
ATL.long: Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

BOS.name: Mitchell Robinson
BOS.note: Robinson (illness) is out for Tuesday's game against Washington, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
BOS.long: With Robinson set to miss a third contest due to an illness, Boston will again be without one of its primary center options. His absence should continue to leave more frontcourt minutes available for Neemias Queta and Luka Garza on Tuesday, with the former being in line to see the lion's share of the playing time.

BKN.name: Nolan Traore
BKN.note: Traore will be re-evaluated in approximately 8-10 weeks due to a right hamstring strain, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
BKN.long: Traore had a productive start to his second year in the NBA, though he's now set to miss an extended period after sustaining a hamstring injury in Friday's loss to Orlando. With the 20-year-old point guard sidelined, Egor Demin, Mikel Brown and Keon Ellis are candidates for increased playing time.

CHA.name: Ryan Kalkbrenner
CHA.note: Kalkbrenner (hip) is doubtful to play Wednesday against the Bulls.
CHA.long: Kalkbrenner suffered the hip injury during Monday's 117-111 loss to the Bulls and is now in danger of missing Wednesday's game. If he's out, Hannes Steinbach will have a chance to get into the rotation.

CHA.name: Dennis Schroder
CHA.note: Schroder (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game the Bulls.
CHA.long: Schroder remains out indefinitely with a hamstring strain. With Charlotte already eliminated from knockout-round contention in the NBA Cup, it's possible the veteran's point guard's absence extends into mid-December.

CHA.name: Sion James
CHA.note: James is probable for Wednesday's game against the Bulls due to general soreness.
CHA.long: James is experiencing some soreness on the left side of his body, but he's expected to power through it Wednesday. James is averaging 5.8 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.1 triples per game this season.

CHA.name: Grayson Allen
CHA.note: Allen (concussion) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game versus Chicago.
CHA.long: Allen has missed the last three games. While it appears he's working toward returning, he's not a lock to get back on the floor Wednesday against the Bulls. If Allen remains on the shelf, Sion James (thigh) and Christian Anderson may continue to see more minutes.

CHA.name: Kon Knueppel
CHA.note: Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
CHA.long: Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

CHI.name: Jalen Smith
CHI.note: Smith (illness) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Hornets.
CHI.long: Smith has been a regular on the injury report recently due to a gastrointestinal illness, though he played in Chicago's last two outings, averaging 18.5 points, 5.0 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.0 combined steals-plus-blocks in 29.5 minutes per contest over that brief stretch. If the big man is unable to play Wednesday, Nic Claxton would likely enter the first unit.

CHI.name: Norman Powell
CHI.note: Powell has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated later this week.
CHI.long: Powell sustained the hamstring injury in Friday's loss to the Wizards and is now set to miss at least the next two contests. With the veteran swingman on the shelf, Isaac Okoro, Buddy Hield, Tre Jones and Patrick Williams are all candidates for increased playing time.

CHI.name: Caleb Wilson
CHI.note: Wilson (hand) is expected to miss four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
CHI.long: The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

CLE.name: Nae'Qwan Tomlin
CLE.note: Tomlin (back) will remain on the inactive list for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
CLE.long: Tomlin, who is recovering from a lower back stress reaction, has yet to suit up for the Cavs this season. He continues to get ruled out 24 hours in advance of tipoff, indicating he's still not close, so he can be viewed as week-to-week moving forward.

CLE.name: Evan Mobley
CLE.note: Mobley will receive treatment and participate in rehab after the team confirmed a diagnosis of a right great toe sprain, and he'll be re-evaluated in the next 7-to-10 days.
CLE.long: Mobley is set to miss his third straight game Monday since suffering the injury, and he's slated to miss at least the next week while on the mend. The Cavs should have a better idea on when he'll return to the court as he begins to progress through the treatment and rehab phase.

DAL.name: Tobi Lawal
DAL.note: Lawal (groin) is out for Tuesday's game against Denver.
DAL.long: Lawal is slated for a fourth consecutive absence due to a right groin strain. His next opportunity to return will arrive Friday in Phoenix.

DAL.name: Dereck Lively II
DAL.note: Head coach Dusty May said Friday that Lively (foot) is moving well and progressing in his recovery, and the big man told May he's "close" to returning, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports.
DAL.long: Lively hasn't seen game action since Nov. 21, 2025, and he remains without a firm timetable to return after undergoing right foot surgery last December. However, this update suggests that the big man is trending in the right direction.

DAL.name: Sergio de Larrea
DAL.note: De Larrea (knee) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
DAL.long: De Larrea has only played four games during the 2026-27 campaign. There hasn't been any indication of when he will be cleared to return, so he should be considered week-to-week for now.

DAL.name: Tarik Biberovic
DAL.note: Biberovic (heel) is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors.
DAL.long: Biberovic has yet to debut for the Mavs this season due to a right heel bursitis issue, and the fact that he continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff suggests he's still not close. Biberovic should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

DET.name: Cade Cunningham
DET.note: Cunningham (knee) is listed as out for Tuesday's game against Orlando.
DET.long: Cunningham was listed as probable, so his absence for Tuesday's meeting with the Magic is concerning. Head coach J.B. Bickerstaff indicated that the knee has been giving the two-time All-Star some trouble of late, and while he's mostly played through it, he will now miss his second game of the 2026-27 campaign. Without Cunningham, Isaiah Joe will enter the starting lineup.
DET.story: Without Cade Cunningham, Pistons get 21 from Isaiah Joe to hand Magic their first NBA Cup loss

DET.name: Ebuka Okorie
DET.note: The Pistons announced Tuesday that Okorie (oblique) will miss at least two weeks, per Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com.
DET.long: Okorie has been diagnosed with an oblique strain, which he sustained in a G League game. The rookie first-rounder has logged a grand total of 20 minutes across five brief appearances, so his absence doesn't have major fantasy ramifications.

DET.name: Taurean Prince
DET.note: Prince underwent arthroscopic right knee surgery Nov. 18 and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
DET.long: Prince last appeared in a game for Detroit on Nov. 14 and is now set to miss an extended period as he recovers from knee surgery. However, the veteran forward's absence shouldn't significantly impact Detroit's rotation.

DET.name: Duncan Robinson
DET.note: Robinson (quadriceps) is considered day-to-day as he progresses in his rehab, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
DET.long: Robinson will miss a fifth consecutive contest Tuesday due to a left quadriceps strain, though he can be considered questionable for Friday's game against Milwaukee until the Pistons provide an update on his status. Kevin Huerter will likely continue seeing increased playing time for as long as Robinson is sidelined.

DET.name: Jalen Duren
DET.note: Duren (hamstring) is being assigned to the Motor City Cruise on Wednesday for practice as he ramps up for a return, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
DET.long: With Duren still out for Detroit and now progressing to a G League practice assignment, this marks a tangible step forward in his recovery from the right hamstring strain that has kept him sidelined since Oct. 23. The Pistons haven't provided a return timeline, but his return appears to be drawing closer as he increases his activity.
DET.story: Jalen Duren to begin rehab assignment in next step to return from injury

GSW.name: Yaxel Lendeborg
GSW.note: Lendeborg is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Kings with an illness.
GSW.long: The standout rookie is in danger of sitting out for the first time all season. Georges Niang and Gui Santos would be in line for more playing time in the frontcourt if Lendeborg isn't feeling well enough to play.

GSW.name: Brandon Williams
GSW.note: Head coach Steve Kerr said Tuesday that Williams (hamstring) is questionable to play Wednesday against the Kings, per Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area.
GSW.long: It sounds like Williams is closing in on ending an extended absence with a hamstring strain. Will Richard and LJ Cryer figure to have the most to lose from a fantasy standpoint once Williams is cleared to return to action.

GSW.name: Stephen Curry
GSW.note: Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
GSW.long: Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

GSW.name: Kristaps Porzingis
GSW.note: Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball.
GSW.long: Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

GSW.name: Moses Moody
GSW.note: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
GSW.long: Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

GSW.name: Jimmy Butler III
GSW.note: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
GSW.long: Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

IND.name: T.J. McConnell
IND.note: McConnell (hamstring) was recalled from the G League's Noblesville Boom on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
IND.long: After missing Indiana's past two games with left hamstring soreness, McConnell joined the club's G League affiliate for practice Tuesday. The veteran point guard can be considered questionable for Friday's game against Philadelphia until the Pacers provide an update on his progress.

IND.name: Tyrese Haliburton
IND.note: Haliburton (hamstring) was recalled from the G League's Noblesville Boom on Tuesday, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
IND.long: Haliburton joined the Pacers' G League affiliate for practice Tuesday, taking a significant step forward in his recovery from a left hamstring strain. However, Shams Charania of ESPN reported Friday that the star point guard is expected to miss at least two more weeks, so Haliburton isn't expected to return to game action in the near future.

IND.name: Aaron Nesmith
IND.note: Nesmith is out for Monday's game against the Thunder due to right foot soreness.
IND.long: The swingman is sitting out the second leg of this back-to-back set and is likely facing a short-term absence. Nesmith's absence should get Obi Toppin onto the streaming map in fantasy leagues Monday.

IND.name: Larry Nance Jr.
IND.note: Nance exited Monday's game against the Thunder due to a sore right ankle and he will not return, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
IND.long: Nance will have three full days to rest his sore ankle before the Pacers' next game, although with Friday's matchup with the 76ers being the first of a back-to-back set, Nance may need to miss that one as well. Obi Toppin figures to pick up most of Nance's minutes while he's sidelined.

IND.name: Ben Sheppard
IND.note: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
IND.long: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

LAC.name: Bradley Beal
LAC.note: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
LAC.long: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

LAC.name: Jordan Miller
LAC.note: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
LAC.long: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

LAL.name: Austin Reaves
LAL.note: Coach JJ Redick stated Monday that the team is optimistic Reaves (heel) will return for Friday's game against San Antonio, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
LAL.long: Reaves has already been downgraded to out for Monday's clash against Utah, which will mark his fifth straight absence due to a bruised left heel. However, the sharpshooter managed to take part in a stay-ready game earlier in the day Monday and was moving well, per Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register. Reaves figures to be in line to take the court Friday as long as he continues to show progress throughout the week.

MEM.name: Scotty Pippen Jr.
MEM.note: Pippen (back) is out for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
MEM.long: Pippen hasn't been available for Memphis since Oct. 29 due to a lumbar disc herniation and remains without a clear timeline to return. He can be deemed week-to-week going forward, though his absence could extend into mid-December if the Grizzlies don't advance in the NBA Cup.

MEM.name: Cameron Boozer
MEM.note: Boozer (ankle) will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
MEM.long: The rookie standout has been diagnosed with a moderate-grade ankle sprain, and he'll be sidelined for at least the next month or so. It's a tough blow for an upstart Grizzlies team, which will now rely even more heavily on Ty Jerome's playmaking for the foreseeable future. Taylor Hendricks has a chance to nail down a consistent role off the bench as well.

MEM.name: Jerami Grant
MEM.note: Grant was diagnosed with a grade 1 left calf strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks.
MEM.long: Grant suffered the injury during Thursday's 126-98 victory over Golden State. He will now be sidelined for at least two weeks, with the team expected to provide an update on his condition at that time. While Grant is on the shelf, Taylor Hendricks and Kris Murray are candidates for more minutes.

MEM.name: GG Jackson
MEM.note: Jackson underwent a procedure Wednesday to repair a broken fifth metatarsal in his left foot. He is expected to recover fully and will be re-evaluated in approximately three months.
MEM.long: Jackson suffered a foot injury in Saturday's 129-110 win over the Nets. Head coach Tuomas Iisalo indicated after the game that the injury was "relatively serious," though it is now confirmed he will miss extended time. While Jackson is out of commission, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant should receive more playing time.

MEM.name: Richie Saunders
MEM.note: Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
MEM.long: Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

MIA.name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
MIA.note: Antetokounmpo (groin) is questionable for Wednesday's game in Philadelphia.
MIA.long: Antetokounmpo missed Sunday's 123-113 win over the Thunder due to right groin tendinitis, but he was able to get through most of Tuesday's practice, so he's trending in the right direction. If he's cleared to return, Bobby Portis would likely head back to the second unit.

MIN.name: Donte DiVincenzo
MIN.note: DiVincenzo (Achilles) has been cleared for team basketball activities and is targeting a return to game action in January, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
MIN.long: DiVincenzo suffered a ruptured right Achilles in late April but is seemingly ahead of schedule in his recovery. With the veteran guard and Anthony Edwards (knee) both sidelined, Bones Hyland and Terrence Shannon figure to continue seeing increased playing time.
MIN.story: Sources: Wolves' Donte DiVincenzo eyes New Year's for season debut

MIN.name: Jaylen Clark
MIN.note: Clark (hamstring) has been ruled out for the next two weeks.
MIN.long: Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday's 117-106 loss to Chicago. He played three minutes as a result of the injury, and he's now slated to miss at least two weeks and will be re-evaluated at that time. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland will see increased playing time off the bench in Clark's absence.

MIN.name: Anthony Edwards
MIN.note: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
MIN.long: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.
MIN.story: LaMelo Ball and the 'collective' carrying Minnesota without Anthony Edwards

NOP.name: Julian Reese
NOP.note: The Pelicans transferred Reese from the G League's Laketown Squadron, and he will be available for New Orleans' game against the Warriors on Monday.
NOP.long: Reese dropped a 15-point, 15-rebound double-double in the Squadron's win over the Mexico City Capitanes on Saturday and will return to the parent club ahead of its game Monday. Through five regular-season appearances at the NBA level this season, the big man is averaging 1.2 points and 1.0 rebounds in 5.4 minutes per tilt.

NOP.name: Trendon Watford
NOP.note: Watford (ankle) is out for Saturday's game against the Spurs.
NOP.long: Watford can be considered week-to-week at this point until the Pelicans offer an update on his recovery. He hasn't played since Nov. 8 and is averaging just 7.2 points and 3.5 boards per game in his six appearances off the bench.

NOP.name: Bennedict Mathurin
NOP.note: Mathurin (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder.
NOP.long: Mathurin will miss a fourth straight contest due to plantar fasciitis in his left foot, which tends to be a lingering injury. Jordan Poole should remain in the backcourt rotation for the undermanned Pelicans moving forward, while Mathurin can be deemed week-to-week.

NOP.name: Dejounte Murray
NOP.note: Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis.
NOP.long: This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

NYK.name: Miles McBride
NYK.note: McBride (adductor) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game versus Cleveland.
NYK.long: McBride could miss a second straight game due to left adductor tightness, though he was able to participate in Tuesday's practice. If the 26-year-old guard remains sidelined, Tyler Kolek, Jose Alvarado and Pacome Dadiet would be candidates for increased playing time.

NYK.name: Jordan Clarkson
NYK.note: Clarkson (foot) is out for Wednesday's game against Cleveland.
NYK.long: The veteran guard is missing a fourth consecutive contest with plantar fasciitis in his right foot. Clarkson didn't practice Tuesday and lacks a timeline for his return.

NYK.name: Josh Hart
NYK.note: Hart (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Cleveland.
NYK.long: Hart is dealing with a right shoulder sprain after dropping a triple-double in Sunday's win over Indiana. If the veteran wing joins OG Anunoby (calf) on the inactive list Wednesday, Mohamed Diawara and Pacome Dadiet would be candidates for an uptick in minutes.

NYK.name: OG Anunoby
NYK.note: Anunoby (calf) is out for Wednesday's game against Cleveland.
NYK.long: Wednesday marks a third consecutive absence for Anunoby, who was unable to practice Tuesday because of a sore left calf. His continued void in the lineup should keep Landry Shamet in the streaming conversation in most fantasy leagues Wednesday.

NYK.name: Karl-Anthony Towns
NYK.note: Towns (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Cleveland.
NYK.long: Towns is at risk of sitting out for the second time in New York's last three contests. Andre Drummond would be a plug-and-play fantasy option at center in most settings if Towns is ultimately unable to play Wednesday.

OKC.name: Nikola Topic
OKC.note: Topic (hip) is listed as out for Wednesday's game versus Minnesota.
OKC.long: Topic has appeared in only three games for the Thunder this season. He's missed the last three contests because of a hip strain, with his next opportunity to suit up coming Saturday in Milwaukee. Without Topic, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix could continue to receive more playing time.

OKC.name: Jaylin Williams
OKC.note: Williams (back) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against Minnesota.
OKC.long: Williams has only played twice in the Thunder's last 11 games. It's unclear when he will be available to return, though his next opportunity to suit up will come Saturday in Milwaukee. With Aday Mara (shin) also ruled out, Kenrich Williams and Micah Peavy should both see more action versus the Timberwolves.

OKC.name: Aday Mara
OKC.note: Mara (leg) is out for Wednesday's game versus the Timberwolves.
OKC.long: This will be Mara's third straight game on the inactive list, and for now, he should be considered questionable at best for Saturday's game in Milwaukee. With Jaylin Williams (back) also unavailable, Micah Peavy and Kenrich Williams will help back up Isaiah Hartenstein at the center position.

OKC.name: Jalen Williams
OKC.note: Williams (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pacers, according to the NBA's official injury report.
OKC.long: Williams remains sidelined following left ankle surgery, with no confirmed return date. His continued absence leaves Oklahoma City without a key offensive contributor, allowing additional opportunities for the Thunder's remaining perimeter players.

OKC.name: Thomas Sorber
OKC.note: Sorber underwent an arthroscopic knee procedure Tuesday to address inflammation at the patellofemoral joint in his right knee, and he's expected to return to on-court activities in 6-8 weeks, Steve McGehee of News 9 Oklahoma City reports.
OKC.long: Once Sorber begins on-court work, there will be a ramp-up period before he's cleared for game-time action, so his absence will likely extend well beyond this initial 6-8-week window. Sorber was selected by the Thunder with the No. 15 pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, but he missed his entire rookie season after tearing the ACL in his right knee and has yet to play this season due to right knee issues.

OKC.name: Cason Wallace
OKC.note: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
OKC.long: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

OKC.name: Chet Holmgren
OKC.note: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
OKC.long: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

ORL.name: Jonathan Isaac
ORL.note: Isaac (knee) is out for Sunday's game against the Wizards.
ORL.long: Isaac continues to deal with a knee injury that has kept him out of action for the entire 2026-27 season. He should continue to be considered week to week until the Magic offer an update on his recovery process.

ORL.name: Izaiyah Nelson
ORL.note: Head coach Sean Sweeney said Wednesday that Nelson (ankle) has been doing "some on-court stuff," though Sweeney added that the work has been "minimal," Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
ORL.long: Nelson underwent surgery this offseason to repair a fractured left ankle. It's encouraging to hear that he's made some progress, but the two-way player can still be considered week-to-week moving forward.

ORL.name: Noah Penda
ORL.note: Penda (hamstring) is making progress but remains without a timetable to return to game action, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
ORL.long: Penda suffered a partially torn hamstring in the preseason and can still be considered week-to-week moving forward. With the second-year forward and Paolo Banchero (ankle) both sidelined, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain should continue seeing increased minutes.

ORL.name: Paolo Banchero
ORL.note: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
ORL.long: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

PHI.name: Joel Embiid
PHI.note: Embiid (illness) is listed as doubtful for Wednesday's game versus Miami.
PHI.long: Embiid missed Monday's 128-111 loss to Portland and doesn't appear to be on track to return Wednesday against the Heat. As a result, Jabari Walker could make another start, with more minutes available for Adem Bona and Dominick Barlow.

PHI.name: Ariel Hukporti
PHI.note: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
PHI.long: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

PHX.name: Mark Williams
PHX.note: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
PHX.long: This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

POR.name: Chris Youngblood
POR.note: Youngblood (heel) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Knicks.
POR.long: Youngblood has been on the shelf since Nov. 10 due to a right heel bone bruise. Until Portland signals otherwise, Youngblood can be considered out indefinitely moving forward.

POR.name: Vit Krejci
POR.note: Krejci underwent surgery on his fractured left ankle Wednesday and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
POR.long: Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

POR.name: Ja Morant
POR.note: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
POR.long: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

POR.name: Shaedon Sharpe
POR.note: Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
POR.long: It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

SAC.name: Maxime Raynaud
SAC.note: Raynaud (knee) was assigned to the G League's Stockton Kings on Wednesday, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
SAC.long: Raynaud is presumably joining the G League Kings for practice, which is an encouraging sign in his recovery from a right patellar subluxation. Until the big man is cleared to return, Dylan Cardwell and Precious Achiuwa are candidates for more minutes.

SAC.name: Ben Simmons
SAC.note: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
SAC.long: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

SAS.name: De'Aaron Fox
SAS.note: Fox (shin) is questionable to play Wednesday's game against the Trail Blazers.
SAS.long: Fox sat out Monday's 123-107 win over Sacramento due to a right shin contusion, and he's now in danger of missing a second consecutive regular-season outing with the ailment. Stephon Castle will continue to see increased usage if Fox remains sidelined.
SAS.story: Fantasy notebook: Karabell on Paul George, Tyler Herro, De'Aaron Fox, more

SAS.name: Victor Wembanyama
SAS.note: Wembanyama (back) is questionable for Wednesday's game in Portland.
SAS.long: Wembanyama sat out Monday's 123-107 win over the Kings due to a back issue, but it looks like he could be back in action Wednesday night. If he's cleared to return, Luke Kornet would head back to the second unit and Tarris Reed could drop from the rotation entirely.

SAS.name: Dylan Harper
SAS.note: Harper (hip) is expected to miss two to three weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
SAS.long: Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip external rotator strain, and San Antonio is now set to be without one of its regular guards for an extended stretch. His absence creates more backcourt minutes for the Spurs, likely most prominently for Justin Champagnie while the team waits for Tobias Harris (calf) to make his season debut. De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle should see extra ball-handling duties as well.
SAS.story: Castle helps Spurs stay unbeaten on road with 123-107 win over Kings minus Wemby, Fox and Harper

SAS.name: Tobias Harris
SAS.note: Harris (calf) is likely to be sidelined until early December, per Jeff Garcia of KENS 5 San Antonio.
SAS.long: Chris Haynes of NBA TV reported Friday that Harris is expected to ramp up his activity this week, and that the veteran forward could make his season debut as soon as early December. Until Harris is finally cleared to return from a calf strain, Julian Champagnie should continue to handle an expanded role on the wing.

SAS.name: Jayden Quaintance
SAS.note: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
SAS.long: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

TOR.name: Kawhi Leonard
TOR.note: Leonard has begun individual on-court workouts following treatment to address swelling in his left knee, and he will be re-evaluated in one week, Marc J. Spears of ESPN.com reports.
TOR.long: Leonard continues to progress in his recovery, and the Raptors are expected to provide another update in a week. Collin Murray-Boyles and Allen Graves will likely continue seeing increased burn for as long as Leonard is sidelined.
TOR.story: Kawhi Leonard's return from knee swelling still at least week away

TOR.name: Nate Bittle
TOR.note: Bittle (foot) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bucks, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports.
TOR.long: Bittle continues to work his way back from a fractured right foot, as he's yet to make his 2026-27 season debut. He remains week-to-week until Toronto provides a definitive update.

TOR.name: RJ Barrett
TOR.note: Barrett has been diagnosed with a right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
TOR.long: Based on his re-evaluation timeline, Barrett likely won't return to game action until mid-December at the earliest. Jamison Battle, Allen Graves and Jamal Shead are candidates for increased playing time in Barrett's absence, especially while Kawhi Leonard (knee) is also sidelined.

UTA.name: Jaxson Hayes
UTA.note: Hayes (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Lakers.
UTA.long: Hayes left Sunday's tilt against the Mavericks with what's now being described as a left knee strain, and it's not yet known how much time he may miss beyond Monday. Mo Bamba should start at center for the Jazz and is worthy of streaming consideration in all fantasy leagues.

UTA.name: Jusuf Nurkic
UTA.note: Nurkic (foot) has been cleared for on-court work and will be re-evaluated in one week.
UTA.long: Nurkic continues to make progress in his recovery from a partial plantar plate tear of the second toe on his right foot, and getting cleared for on-court work is a big step in his rehab. There are still a few steps he'll need to clear before he makes his return to the floor, but once he's able to get through full-contact, 5-on-5 work, we'll know he's close.

UTA.name: Lauri Markkanen
UTA.note: Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
UTA.long: Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

UTA.name: Jaren Jackson Jr.
UTA.note: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
UTA.long: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

WAS.name: Tristan Vukcevic
WAS.note: Vukcevic (hip) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against Boston.
WAS.long: Vukcevic has yet to suit up this season due to a left hip injury. He can be considered week-to-week until the Wizards provide an update on his progress.

WAS.name: Reece Beekman
WAS.note: The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks.
WAS.long: Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

WAS.name: Justin Champagnie
WAS.note: Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
WAS.long: The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

WAS.name: Jamir Watkins
WAS.note: The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL.
WAS.long: Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.
